cleanIntro: The Howa Model 1500 is a push-feed bolt gun with an internal box magazine and a hinged floor plate, and its field strip is exactly two things: get the bolt out, and if you are going further, get the barrelled action out of the stock. Howa Machinery builds it; this book is the one Legacy Sports International publishes and services in the US, and it sends warranty work to LSI. Two safety patterns exist on this rifle — a two-position lever and a three-position lever that also locks the bolt shut — so check which one is on your receiver before you try to open the action with the safety on. The trigger is sealed at the factory and is not part of any cleaning you do.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, safety ON, then open it
steps.action: Point it somewhere that would not matter if it fired, and leave the safety ON while you work the bolt — on the Howa the safety can stay engaged during unloading on the two-position pattern. Lift the bolt handle and draw the bolt back gently rather than snatching it; a gentle pull lets the extractor lift a live round out cleanly instead of flicking it into the receiver wall. Leave the bolt open when the round is out.
steps.prose: This is the manual's own first instruction, printed ahead of the magazine work, because a rifle with a live round still in the chamber is not made safe by emptying the magazine.
steps.quote: 1. Point the rifle in a safe direction! The safety should be kept "ON"!
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Unloading, p.19

steps.title: Dump the magazine through the floor plate, not through the chamber
steps.action: Cup a hand under the floor plate to catch it, then press the floor plate catch just ahead of the trigger guard. The plate is hinged and spring-loaded by the magazine follower, so it will drop open and throw the whole column of cartridges into your palm — if you do not have a hand there they hit the bench. Look into the magazine well and the chamber afterwards; do not take an empty-feeling rifle on trust.
steps.prose: The floor plate route is the one Howa insists on. Cycling the bolt to empty the magazine feeds every remaining round through the chamber, which is exactly the state you were trying to get out of.
steps.quote: 3. Empty the magazine from below (Fig. 9). Hold one hand loosely under the floor plate to restrain it, and depress the floor plate catch (4).
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Unloading, p.19
steps.warn: 2. It is recommended that you always empty the magazine by the method described above. Do not empty the magazine by cycling the bolt, since this process involves feeding cartridges into the chamber, and introduces an additional risk of an accidental firing.

steps.title: Model 1500 magazine capacity is caliber-dependent — count what came out
steps.action: Know how many rounds should have fallen into your hand before you decide the rifle is empty. The Model 1500's internal box holds five in standard calibers, three in magnums and six in .223, so a magnum rifle that gave up five cartridges has just told you something is wrong with your count, not with the rifle. Count them, then look into the box anyway.
steps.prose: Capacity varies with the cartridge because the same box is fitted with a spacer in .223 and swallows fatter magnum cases in smaller numbers.
steps.caution: Capacity is a Model 1500 figure that changes with chambering: 5 standard, 3 magnum, 6 in .223.
steps.quote: 2. Press cartridges down into the magazine one at a time as shown in Fig. 5 until the magazine is full (5 cartridges in standard calibers, 3 in magnum calibers, 6 in .223 caliber).
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Loading, p.17

steps.title: Look in the chamber — a case can stay put
steps.action: With the bolt back, put your eye on the chamber mouth and confirm you can see bare steel. A case that has been fired hot, or one seated in a fouled chamber, can grip hard enough that the extractor slips off its rim and leaves it behind while the bolt comes back empty. Feeling the chamber with a finger is a fair second check, but the manual asks for a look.
steps.prose: Howa calls this rare and then tells you to check anyway, which is the correct weighting for something that only has to happen once.
steps.quote: 1. Always LOOK in the chamber to make sure the cartridge has been extracted and the chamber is empty. It is rare for a cartridge to remain stuck in the chamber, but it can happen.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Unloading, Warning, p.19

steps.title: Which safety is on your Model 1500 — two-position or three
steps.action: Look at the knurled lever on the right of the receiver behind the bolt handle. On the two-position rifle the lever has a forward FIRE position and a rear SAFE position that locks the trigger, and the bolt can still be lifted. On the three-position rifle the fully rearward notch locks the BOLT as well, so if the handle will not lift with the safety back, you have the three-position lever and you must bring it to the middle detent to open the action.
steps.prose: This is the single control difference most likely to make an owner think their rifle is broken during a strip. It is a variant of the Model 1500, not a different rifle.
steps.quote: The safety on the Model 1500 rifle consists of a knurled lever on the right side of the receiver immediately to the rear of the bolt handle. When "ON", it locks the trigger.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Use of the Safety: Two Position, p.12
steps.warn: 3. The safety is "ON" when the lever is pushed fully rearward, covering the red indicator dot. In this position, the bolt is locked and cannot be opened.

steps.title: Bolt out of the receiver
steps.action: Lift the bolt handle, draw the bolt part way back, then press the bolt stop on the left rear of the receiver and pull the bolt straight out. The bolt stop is the small lever the bolt snaps past on the way in; hold it depressed for the whole withdrawal or the bolt will jam against it halfway. Set the bolt down on its side, not on its face, so the extractor and ejector are not carrying the weight.
steps.prose: The manual states this relationship from the installing end — the bolt goes in until the stop snaps in place behind it — and removal is that snap released deliberately.
steps.aside: The disassembly page of this printing (p.21) is set in a double-struck display face that machine extraction cannot read cleanly, so the quotation above is taken from the manual's matching reassembly instruction on p.26.
steps.quote: Push the bolt forward gently into the receiver until the bolt stop snaps in place behind it. Close the bolt and turn the handle down to its locked position.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Reassembly, To install bolt in rifle, p.26

steps.title: Barrelled action out of the stock — rear screw first
steps.action: Lay the rifle on something padded and use a screwdriver that actually fills the slot. Take out the takedown screw behind the trigger guard first, then the one in front of it, then lift the trigger guard away and separate stock from action. The magazine box is loose once the guard is off — lift it out and note that its open end faces rearward and its notched end goes in first.
steps.prose: The two screws are different lengths. The longer one lives behind the trigger guard, and putting them back the other way round bottoms a screw in the wrong hole.
steps.quote: 2. To replace stock: Insert magazine box into receiver, open end to the rear and notched end first. Place barreled action assembly carefully into stock. Be certain trigger guard is seated properly in stock. The longer takedown screw goes behind the trigger guard.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Reassembly, To replace stock, p.26
steps.warn: WARNING: Do not screw in trigger guard when bolt is in gun.

steps.title: The trigger is sealed — leave it alone
steps.action: You will see adjustment screws on the trigger housing once the action is out of the stock. Do not touch them. On the Model 1500 the safety acts directly on the trigger mechanism, so moving a trigger screw can leave the safety unable to block the sear, and Howa treats a broken seal as grounds to send the rifle back rather than shoot it.
steps.prose: This is why the strip stops here on a rifle whose trigger looks so accessible with the stock off.
steps.quote: The safety operates directly on the trigger mechanism. For this reason, the trigger adjustments have been sealed at the factory. Any attempt to change these adjustments may render the safety inoperative and create a hazardous condition.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Use of the Safety, Warning, p.13

steps.title: Bore and chamber go back DRY
steps.action: Whatever solvent or oil you put down the Model 1500's bore comes out again before a cartridge goes in. Run dry patches from the breech until they come out clean and dry, and wipe the chamber walls specifically. Oil left in the chamber stops the case gripping the wall as it should, which throws bolt thrust the action was never meant to take, and any incompressible film in the bore is a pressure event waiting for the next shot.
steps.prose: This is the one cleaning instruction the manual states as a safety requirement rather than as care.
steps.quote: 5. Before loading, always clean all grease, oil, solvent, etc. from the bore and chamber.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Loading, Warning 5, p.16
steps.warn: Any lubricant film in the chamber interferes with the adhesion between case and chamber wall that is necessary for safe firing.

steps.title: After an obstruction, clean before you shoot again
steps.action: If you ever tap a lodged bullet out of the barrel, the job is not finished when the bullet falls out. Unburned powder and fouling stay behind in the bore, the chamber and the receiver, and the rifle does not go back into service until all of it is scrubbed out. Use a brass rod that fits the bore for the bullet itself — a cleaning rod will bend and add a second obstruction to the first.
steps.prose: Mud, snow and debris in the muzzle get the same treatment: rod them out, never shoot them out.
steps.quote: It is imperative that the bore, chamber, and receiver be thoroughly cleaned to remove all such residue before shooting is resumed.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Bore Obstructions (continued), p.11
steps.warn: Soil, mud, snow, water, ice, vegetation, mudwasp nests, etc. are all dangerous inside a gun barrel.

steps.title: The bolt leaves the rifle as one piece — that is the limit
steps.action: For a field strip the Model 1500 bolt comes out whole and stays whole. If you are tempted to twist the back off it while it is in your hand, know where that stops: the bolt sleeve and firing pin are a semi-permanent assembly under full mainspring load, and Howa puts anything beyond removing that unit behind a gunsmith with the right tools. Wipe the body, the lugs and the bolt face and put it down.
steps.prose: Deep Clean covers rotating that sleeve off when oil has got into the bolt. Even there the assembly itself does not come apart.
steps.quote: The bolt sleeve/firing pin assembly is a semipermanent assembly and should not be disassembled except by a gunsmith. These parts are under heavy spring pressure which could cause injury if improperly disassembled without the use of special tools that are required.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Bolt Disassembly & Reassembly, Warning, p.23

steps.title: Dry firing the Model 1500 is not a pastime
steps.action: You will snap it once as part of the function check after the bolt goes back in, and that is expected. What Howa rules out is repeated dry firing, because on this rifle nothing arrests the firing pin and it takes the whole blow every time. If you want to let the mainspring down without snapping it, lift the bolt handle, hold the trigger back and lower the handle again — the rifle uncocks quietly.
steps.prose: Never do that with a cartridge in the chamber; it leaves the pin resting on a live primer, which is the one condition this manual calls unsafe outright.
steps.caution: 4. Never uncock the rifle with a cartridge in the chamber.
steps.quote: Extensive dry firing (snapping the firing mechanism without a cartridge in the chamber) is not recommended as it may result in breakage of the firing pin.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Firing, p.20

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Bolt out, magazine empty, and — if you went that far — the barrelled action out of the stock with the magazine box beside it. That is the whole of the strip Howa publishes for the Model 1500. Deep Clean covers the bolt teardown, which is the sleeve and firing pin assembly rotating off the back of the bolt body, and the hard limit on how far that goes.
steps.prose: Whatever you did, the rifle does not get ammunition again until the function check below has been done — an incorrectly reassembled bolt is the failure mode this manual warns about most bluntly.
steps.quote: Attempting to reinstall an incorrectly assembled bolt with a cartridge in the rifle may, under unusual conditions, cause the cartridge to fire accidentally as the bolt is being closed, without the trigger being pressed. Serious injury to the shooter could result.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Reassembly, Warning, p.26

deepSteps.title: Most of the time, don't
deepSteps.action: Howa's position is that the bolt rarely needs taking apart, because brushing and wiping its outside handles routine fouling. Pull it down when oil has crept inside and the firing pin has gone sluggish, or after a soaking, and not as a habit. Every teardown is another chance to reassemble it uncocked or with the firing pin protruding.
deepSteps.prose: That judgement is worth respecting on a rifle whose bolt has no service-adjustable parts inside it.
deepSteps.quote: It is seldom necessary to dismantle the bolt, as
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Bolt Disassembly & Reassembly, p.23

deepSteps.title: Bolt sleeve and firing pin off the back — and no further
deepSteps.action: Hold the bolt with its rear face towards you and rotate the bolt sleeve and firing pin assembly about a third of a turn clockwise until it releases, then draw it straight off rearward. That assembly is where you stop. It is a semi-permanent unit under heavy mainspring load, and Howa puts it behind a gunsmith and special tools rather than behind care.
deepSteps.prose: If the sleeve rotates too far during handling the cocking piece snaps forward to uncocked; that is recoverable, but only by re-cocking it against the detent notch, not by forcing anything.
deepSteps.quote: The bolt sleeve/firing pin assembly is a semipermanent assembly and should not be disassembled except by a gunsmith. These parts are under heavy spring pressure which could cause injury if improperly disassembled without the use of special tools that are required.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Bolt Disassembly & Reassembly, Warning, p.23

deepSteps.title: Brush the bolt exterior, then rebuild it hard
deepSteps.action: Clean the bolt body, lugs and bolt face, then start the sleeve back on with its small lug lined up with the slot in the bolt. Push it in until it stops, then keep pushing hard — it has to bottom against the rear face of the bolt before it will turn — and rotate it counter-clockwise about a third of a turn until you feel a distinct click. That click is the cocking piece nose dropping into its detent notch, and it is the only confirmation you get.
deepSteps.prose: If you cannot feel the click, the sleeve is not bottomed. Pressing harder is the fix, not turning harder.
deepSteps.quote: the slot (B) in the bolt hole and slide the bolt sleeve/firing pin assembly into the bolt until it stops. Applying heavy pressure, continue pushing the bolt sleeve/firing pin assembly forward until the bolt sleeve bottoms against the rear face of the bolt. While holding it in firmly, rotate the bolt sleeve/firing pin assembly counter-clockwise about 1/3 turn until a slight click is felt.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Bolt Disassembly & Reassembly, To reassemble, p.23

deepSteps.title: Look at the bolt face before it goes back in
deepSteps.action: Turn the bolt around and look at the front. The firing pin tip must be retracted inside its hole — if it is standing proud, the bolt is uncocked or wrongly assembled and it must not go into the rifle. A protruding pin on a chambered round is the mechanism by which a bolt-closure discharge happens.
deepSteps.prose: Howa illustrates this as correct-versus-incorrect on facing figures because it is the one check that catches every reassembly error at once.
deepSteps.quote: the front face of the bolt (Figs. 14 and 15): the tip of the firing pin (E) should be retracted, and not
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Bolt Disassembly & Reassembly, p.23
deepSteps.warn: A firing pin protruding through the firing pin hole is INCORRECT ASSEMBLY.

deepSteps.title: The bolt must go back cocked
deepSteps.action: A correctly reassembled Model 1500 bolt is cocked, with the rectangular projection of the cocking piece pointing straight down at six o'clock when you view it from the rear. That orientation is what lets the lugs line up with their races and the bolt slide home. An uncocked bolt will fight you at the receiver mouth — do not push harder, re-cock it.
deepSteps.prose: Hooking the cocking piece on the corner of a bench and drawing it back while turning the sleeve is the manual's own recovery for a bolt that snapped forward.
deepSteps.quote: The firing pin will now be in the cocked position, where it must be in order for the bolt to be correctly reinstalled in the rifle.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION & SAFETY MANUAL — READ CAREFULLY BEFORE USING THIS FIREARM — HOWA SERIES 1500 RIFLES — ABSENT — no revision, part number or print code is printed anywhere in the document — Bolt Disassembly & Reassembly, p.23

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Clean from the breech end with a rod that fits, and finish with dry patches
Remove every trace of grease, oil and solvent from bore and chamber before loading
After any bore obstruction, scrub bore, chamber AND receiver before shooting again
Rod out mud, snow or debris — never attempt to shoot an obstruction out

cleaning.name: BOLT
tasks: Routine: brush and wipe the exterior, the lugs and the bolt face; no teardown needed
Strip the bolt only if oil has penetrated it or it has been soaked
Stop at the bolt sleeve/firing pin assembly — gunsmith only beyond that point
Confirm the firing pin tip is retracted at the bolt face before reinstalling

cleaning.name: ACTION & STOCK
tasks: With the action out, wipe the receiver, magazine box and floor plate
Do NOT touch the sealed trigger adjustment screws
Refit the magazine box open-end rearward, notched end first
Never run the trigger guard screws home with the bolt still in the rifle

reassembly: Refit the magazine box into the receiver, open end to the rear and notched end first.
Seat the barrelled action in the stock with the trigger guard properly located, remembering the LONGER takedown screw goes behind the trigger guard.
Tighten both takedown screws alternately until snug, then tighten the front screw firmly, then the rear.
With the bolt OUT of the rifle for this step — never screw the trigger guard in with the bolt in the gun.
Orient the bolt handle up and to the right, lugs aligned with their races and the cocking piece projection at six o'clock, and push it in until the bolt stop snaps behind it.
Close the bolt and turn the handle down to its locked position.
fncheck: Any time the bolt has been out, do this before ammunition goes anywhere near the rifle: "Push the safety "OFF". Press the trigger. The firing pin should snap forward ("dry-fire"). Operate the bolt again a full cycle. It should close smoothly and turn down to lock easily, without impediment. If either does not, the bolt may be incorrectly assembled." (Reassembly, Warning, p.26). Also confirm the safety still locks the trigger in the ON position, and on a three-position lever that the fully rearward notch locks the bolt shut. A rifle that fails either check goes to LSI, not to the range.
